method: GF+ adaptive per-row format selection on REAL trained weights (webterm_gfplus v2 6fb1863, linear layers, 43520 rows)
cross_replication: gfplus_pod_benchmark.py (independent implementation, all 39 2D matrices incl. embeddings, same checkpoint): 4bit 19.46, 6bit 31.09, 8bit 43.24, 16bit 91.44 — ordering identical, divergence <= 0.09 dB. See research/GFPLUS_CROSS_REPLICATION.md
key_finding: Invariant holds in all classes: GF+A >= best single pocket (+0.01..+0.08 dB). Pocket selection with CORRECT full-scale: 4-bit nf4 95%, 6-bit phi-e2m3 89% (phi split = best single pocket of the class), 8-bit e2m5 87%; INT is a minority pocket (int8 5.9% of rows). Narrow-exponent floats (e2) win all classes >= 8 bit in per-row-scale mode; wide exponents (e4m3/fp16/bf16) idle.
honest_limitation: MSE/SQNR-level only, NOT downstream BPB; QAT unverified; margins on homogeneous weights are small (+0.01..+0.08 dB) and do NOT pay for the 2-bit/row header vs the best fixed pocket on THIS model — adaptive value = insurance on heterogeneous/heavy-tailed data (testA/C). phi-split is best single at 6-bit but loses to e2m5 at 8-bit and e2m13 at 16-bit in scaled mode.
retraction_note: v1 of this file (commit 22bf31e) recorded numbers from a buggy run (webterm_gfplus v1): L-inf pocket selection vs MSE report, floats normalized to 1.0 instead of format MAXN (crushed into denormals), mixed aggregations. Its conclusions 'GF+A picks INT in 99.8% of rows', 'float pockets never selected', 'phi-rule not useful with per-row scaling' are ARTIFACTS of those bugs and are RETRACTED; the corrected v2 shows nearly the opposite (float pockets dominate selection at 6/8/16 bit). Do not cite v1 numbers.
